messages:
Maggie: Heads-up — seeing intermittent drops of X-Client-Id on /v1/embeddings traffic after the edge rewrite. Canary shows quota attr pinging fallback model more than usual. Anyone seen header loss tied to rewrite order?
Kevin: Which rewrite chain is applied? gateway -> auth -> proxy?
Sam: Gateway applies path normalization then header transforms, then final proxy rewrite. We had that old rule that strips headers for host normalization, might be too aggressive.
Rachel: Can you paste the offending rule?
Maggie: Yep, found it in the route config for /v1/embeddings. Snippet: 
```yaml
match:
  prefix: /v1/embeddings
rewrite:
  path: /api/embeddings
  headers:
    remove: ["X-Client-Id"]
    set:
      X-Origin: "edge-proxy"
```
Sam: Ah — that remove is unconditional. We probably added it to avoid leaking internal client ids to upstreams during a vendor test. But for our internal auth flow we need X-Client-Id preserved.
Kevin: Two options: make removal conditional on upstream host OR add a preserve list in the gateway that marks headers to not strip when route.metadata.internal_auth == true.
Maggie: I'm leaning to route-level metadata so it's explicit per-route. Less global surprises and easier to audit. Add a QA matrix column for "headers preserved".
Rachel: Implementation note: the current engine applies header removals during canonicalization stage before we attach jwt-derived headers. If we move preserve-check earlier we need to ensure it runs after auth plugin. Might be simpler to run a second pass that prunes header_remove list based on route.flags.
Sam: Agree. Pseudocode: 
```js
// after auth plugin
if (route.flags.preserve_client_id && req.headers['x-client-id']) {
  // remove from header_remove list
  headerRemove = headerRemove.filter(h => h !== 'x-client-id')
}
applyHeaderRemoves(headerRemove)
```
Rachel: Also add an audit tag for telemetry so we can chart how many requests were subject to header-preserve logic. That will help justify the change to security folks.
Maggie: Good call. We should emit a counter metric: gateway.header_preserve{route, env, outcome} with outcome in {preserved, removed}.
Kevin: Small UX ask for Console: route editor should surface "preserve headers" toggle and list which headers are impacted. Product asked for a hover tooltip explaining implications on quotas and upstream logging.
Sam: On testing: add an e2e that hits /v1/embeddings with upstream host variation and asserts X-Client-Id present for internal route flag true and absent otherwise.
Maggie: I'll draft a PR. Plan: 1) route metadata flag + console toggle, 2) header-removal second-pass logic, 3) telemetry counter, 4) e2e and unit tests.
Rachel: Can you also add a short migration note in the changelog about existing routes that currently rely on unconditional removal? We probably need to scan and set the flag for affected routes.
Maggie: Yup — will add a script to list routes with X-Client-Id in removal lists.
deploy-bot: Canary started for "gateway-header-preserve" config (canary=10% traffic) — id: canary-2024-11-09-11.
Kevin: :eyes: I'll monitor the quotas and fallback model hits for the next hour.
Sam: If numbers look good, :shipit: for canary.
Maggie: Thanks, will follow up with PR link and a quick console mock for the toggle.
Rachel: :thumbsup:
